**The highest-leverage line in the whole package**, and the one most often left

I followed `supplier-quote-request`. It needed no other skill. The RFQ package for BSH-1210 is drafted and both bids are read into one shape and compared, but the package can't be released yet. Nothing was sent to any supplier and nothing was awarded.

**Why release is blocked:** the skill has to check the drawing revision against the ERP item master, and no ERP or item-master export was available. The drawing and the MRP demand both say Rev A (2025-06-02), so the check is "unverified", not a mismatch. Document control has to confirm Rev A before the package goes out. No ITAR, EAR or export-control markings were found in the four input files.

**RFQ package (draft):**
- **Demand:** 3,200 pcs over 2026-12 to 2027-02 (800 / 1,200 / 1,200 by month), all at Rev A. No purchase history and no forecast were in the inputs; the package says so instead of leaving the volume out.
- **Quantity breaks:** 800, 1,200 and 3,200. I proposed these from the MRP numbers; the buyer needs to confirm them.
- **Response format:** suppliers must quote a unit price at each break, tooling and who owns it, lead time to first article and to production from a named event, MOQ, currency, validity as a date, and accept or list exceptions to each clause. Bids in another shape get sent back.
- **Placeholders:** due date, first article date, contacts, commercial terms and most quality clauses are left in [brackets]. There was no plant setup on file, so I didn't make them up. The only quality clause on the part record is "certificate of conformance per lot", and the clause set is flagged as unverified.
- **What's kept out:** no prices, no other supplier names and no target price are inside the package. Both the package and every email passed that check.

**The two bids (both off-format, neither supplier confirmed approved, neither bid dated):**
- **Alder (Q-A-118):** quoted Rev A, 0.62 USD at 1,000 pcs and 0.55 at 3,000 pcs. Minimum order 1,000, existing tooling, 4 weeks after order, FOB origin. It lists a hardness exception of 25-45 HRF against the drawing's 25-40. 10 required fields are missing.
- **Birch (BPM-77):** 0.49 USD at 3,200 pcs, plus 1,850 USD one-time tooling. 6-7 weeks with no start event, delivered DDP Dayton, payment net 45. It doesn't say which revision it quoted. 9 required fields are missing.
- **Comparison:** at the proposed breaks, only Birch is priced at one of them (3,200). Each supplier's own quantities were compared too, but not ranked against each other because the quantities and freight terms differ: Alder 1,650.00 USD for 3,000 pcs against Birch 3,418.00 USD for 3,200 pcs including tooling.

**Recommendation (provisional, the buyer decides):** pursue Alder, on conditions. Neither bid is ready for buyer review. Before any award: Rev A confirmed, engineering accepts or rejects the hardness exception, both suppliers restate at 800 / 1,200 / 3,200, supplier approval, a first article date, and one freight basis. Alder's minimum order of 1,000 is above the December need of 800, and its 3,000-pc price leaves 200 pcs unpriced.

**Email drafts:** two RFQ covers and two restatement requests, all marked HELD. The reasons are the revision gate, no due date, no contact emails and no approval status.

**What I could not do:**
- Release the package or send the emails, because of the revision gate.
- Confirm supplier approval or single-source status: there is no approved-supplier table, vendor record or purchase history, so the current price and incumbent are unknown.
- Save Word or Excel copies: python-docx and openpyxl aren't installed, so the documents are only in `reply.md`. That breaks the skill's no-.md-for-documents rule, which I noted.
- Save the tracker to the Open work page or publish the Supply Chain page: artifact tools weren't allowed this run. The tracker is printed in `reply.md` and the Supply Chain page is offered as a file.
